newsitem.title: CHINA: STUDY HONG KONG INSURANCE, CHINESE INSURER SAYS.
newsitem.headline: STUDY HONG KONG INSURANCE, CHINESE INSURER SAYS.

text.p: A newly-founded Chinese insurer has called for the domestic insurance market to study the experience of its capitalist counterpart Hong Kong, the Financial News said on Wednesday.
High commissions and low premiums had slashed profits in China's insurance market, the newspaper quoted Hu Xinmin, deputy general manager of Shenzhen-based Hua An Property Insurance Co, as saying.
Mainland firms should study Hong Kong insurers' experience in cooperating with one another to regularise the market, said Hu, whose firm was established in October last year.

China should learn from Hong Kong insurers' success in developing minimum pricing levels, a standard system of basic insurance and cooperation to guarantee disaster insurance through re-insurance and co-insurance, he said.
Insurers in the British colony, which returns to Chinese rule on July 1, had also cut exchange costs by unifying commissions for intermediaries, he said.

By contrast, over-competition among insurers in the booming southern city of Shenzhen had slashed premiums and raised commissions to suicidal levels, seriously disrupting the market in insurance and restricting its development, he said.
-- Beijing Newsroom (8610) 6532 1921 Wednesday, 11 June 1997 10:49:39 ENDS nPEK00395
